subject: Post-demo recap & proposed eval roadmap — model recommendations + JSON ops
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@helios.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & proposed eval roadmap — model recommendations + JSON ops

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the evaluation plan I promised so we have clear next steps.

Recap (2 min):
- Goal: replace rule-based extraction in Helios CRM with structured output + tool-calling for enrichment (company lookups, revenue normalization).
- Primary constraints: 200–1,200 token payloads, P95 latency target <= 350ms, strong JSON schema pass rate for downstream ingestion.

Proposed evaluation roadmap (week 0–3):
1) Intake & dataset: Helios provides a 500-record sample (anonymized) — we need this to seed prompt sets and schema tests (please send S3 or CSV).
2) Quick-bench (48h): run small-batch latency/cost sweep across 3 model families + quantized variants. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, per-token cost estimate.
3) Schema compliance run (72h): run structured-output tests against your JSON schema (see attached prompt-suite-v1.csv). Measure schema pass rate and common failure modes.
4) Resilience & retry matrix (ongoing): test retries/backoff, max_attempts, and fallback policy to lighter models for degraded P95.

Initial model recommendations to try (start order):
- Redwood-2-7B-q4 (fast, cost-efficient) — candidate for baseline and high-throughput flows
- OpenAssistant-13B (balanced quality) — candidate for higher-fidelity extraction
- Redwood-2-70B-fx (higher-quality, higher-cost) — run on smaller sample for edge cases

Key evaluation artifacts we will share: prompt set (attached), benchmark dashboard link (Drive), per-model JSON pass/fail breakdown. If there are regulatory constraints on sample data, let us know and we can sign the NDA/data sharing addendum.

Asks / next steps:
- Alex: can you share the 500-record sample (helios-sample-500.csv) and the JSON schema for the extraction output by EOD Friday?
- Helios procurement: propose a short call to align on SOW & timeline next week (15–30 min).
- Internal: I’ll spin up the eval harness and post initial bench results in the shared Drive link.

Attachments: Helios_requirements_v2.pdf, prompt-suite-v1.csv

Thanks —
Sean

Internal notes / proposed owners:
- Aditya: own the eval harness run (bench + schema compliance). Deliverable: bench dashboard + JSON pass-rate CSV by 2026-09-10. Use the GitHub eval-harness/helios-2026 branch.
- Laura: lead model recommendation discussion once we have bench numbers; prepare one-slide tradeoff (latency vs cost vs pass rate).
- Monica: own SSO/procurement touchpoint for any enterprise needs (SLA, data handling).

Evaluation matrix (high-level metrics):
- Accuracy: JSON schema pass rate (required >= 95% for core fields)
- Latency: p95 request latency (target <= 350ms)
- Cost: tokens/request and projected $/1M requests
- Resilience: retry success rate and time-to-fallback (should degrade gracefully)

Retry & fallback plan (prototype):
- Max attempts: 3
- Backoff: linear 200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms (circuit open if >10% failures in 5m window)
- Fallback: if p95 > 750ms or schema pass rate drops >10% vs baseline, route to Redwood-2-7B-q4 with relaxed schema enrichment (post-process heuristics).

Please ack and estimate ETA for the first bench run (Aditya).

Thanks —
Sean

Ack — I’ll kick off the eval harness once we get the sample CSV + schema. Quick notes:
- I’ll seed the prompt set with the attached prompt-suite-v1.csv and add 6 paraphrase variants per sample for robustness (will push to GitHub branch).
- Baseline run (3 models x 2 quant configs x 500 records) should take ~18–24 hours once infra is up.
- I’ll instrument schema failure reasons (type mismatch, missing keys, malformed JSON) and tag with example IDs so we can tune prompts.

Questions:
1) Can Helios share a minimal SLA requirement (max acceptable p95 + allowed cost band)? If procurement needs a template SOW, Monica — can you share the standard SOW template?
2) For retries, do we want to attempt tool-calls (external enrichment) on the same attempt or only after schema failure? My suggestion: attempt tool-call only on 2nd attempt to avoid long tail latency on initial responses.

I’ll aim to have the first dashboard link by 2026-09-06 AM Pacific.

—Aditya
